doctrineGuard.risk: The name reads as word-faith. 'Sing it done' can be heard as singing a thing into existence.
doctrineGuard.answer: The tagline is the guard and it is load-bearing: 'Sing what He has already said'. Kernel section 8 holds it — a declaration does not create the thing, it announces what He has already spoken, and what He has spoken is finished before it is seen. Every lyric on this property anchors to the written word inside the line itself, never to the singer's own confidence.

doctrineGuard.rule: No lyric on this property may make receiving conditional on the listener's faith, guarantee an outcome, or imply anyone failed to qualify.

notes: This tenant was created before its catalogue existed, which is the reverse of how the other four came about. Nothing breaks — an empty scope renders an empty catalogue — but do not read a green check-tenants run as evidence that a visitor would see anything.

The manifest category key is `declarations`. On the music drive the albums sit directly under J:/singitdone.com/music with no category folder between. The two are not the same string and nothing should assume they are.
A code prefix is not a tenant boundary. The catalogue scope is the category key, enforced in lib/manifest.ts at load.

Design changed twice on 2026-08-19 before any lyric was approved: twelve voice compilation, then one artist per album. The blueprint gate is what made that cheap. Ten lyric drafts written under the first design were discarded rather than retrofitted.

rulings.testimonyAnchor: REMOVED. Founder ruling 2026-08-19. SOP section 18 requires a Testimony Anchor Track on every Jubilee album; that requirement is set aside for this property. No album here designates one and QA must not flag the absence.
rulings.propheticDeclarationFloor: 95% on the SOP section 5.5 Prophetic Declaration Rule, ten points above the standard 85% delivery target. Founder ruling 2026-08-19.
rulings.register: Declarations sung BEFORE Yahuah with thanksgiving toward Him, spoken over the singer own soul in the pattern of David (1 Samuel 30:6; Psalm 42:5, 103:1, 62:5, 116:7). SOP section 3.6 Vertical Address describes songs sung TO Yahuah and is not applied here as a pass or fail.
rulings.soulAddressBudget: Twice per song. Once at the top to set the posture, once at the close to return to it. Never used as a chorus refrain.
rulings.finishedPossession: Founder ruling 2026-08-19. THE ACT IS STATED IN THE PERFECT; THE STANDING RESULT STAYS PRESENT. He has said it / He has released me / I have hidden it, alongside I walk free / peace is mine. Banned: the future for a finished thing, and the habitual-practice frame for a finished act (I hide it, I keep releasing, I try to) which describes effort in progress and hands the weight back to the singer. Where Scripture uses the perfect, the lyric uses the perfect. Worked example: Psalm 119:11, the verb tsaphanti is Qal perfect 1cs, so it is I have hidden it in my heart, never I hide it.
